findings.location: scripts/native_qualification_v3.py check_record boot-entry rules (lines 239-242), _kernel_params (486-489), MAINTENANCE_TOKEN comment (56); README 'W02e K1: boot entries' row and decision 2; vectors.json V47-V49
findings.finding:
The new token rules split the command line on single spaces and stop at the first bare "--". Neither the kernel nor systemd reads the line that way.
(1) systemd v256 PID 1 on a host reads all of /proc/cmdline. In src/basic/proc-cmdline.c, proc_cmdline_strv_internal splits the line with EXTRACT_UNQUOTE and has no "--" handling on the host path. In src/core/main.c, parse_proc_cmdline_item sets arg_default_unit from every systemd.unit=, and the last one wins. In addition, the kernel's setup_command_line (init/main.c) places bootconfig init.* keys after " -- " in saved_command_line.
- Probe W6-a: ENROLLED is the positive's line plus " -- systemd.unit=planeon-maintenance.target". check_qualification ACCEPTS it with every capture rebound, yet that boot starts the maintenance target.
- Probe W6-d: a MAINTENANCE entry whose token comes after "--" (the bootconfig init.* path) is refused.
(2) The kernel's next_arg (lib/cmdline.c) and systemd both honour double quotes. The model does not.
- Probe W6-b: ENROLLED with 'lockdown=integrity x=" -- " systemd.unit=planeon-maintenance.target' is ACCEPTED, although the kernel and systemd both see the token as a parameter.
- Probe W6-c: 'x=" lockdown=integrity "' passes the lockdown test. The observed hardening.lockdown value still covers the actual state.
- Probe W6-h: '"lockdown=integrity"' is refused, although the kernel applies it.
(3) Probe W6-e: a MAINTENANCE entry 'systemd.unit=planeon-maintenance.target systemd.unit=multi-user.target' is ACCEPTED, although systemd boots multi-user.target.
Every capture hash-binds the /proc/cmdline text, so this is an analysis error on observed data. It defeats the rule's stated purpose ('the enrolled entry never does'), and W02e K1 ties the maintenance window to exactly this systemd target. The discriminator itself, two different entry IDs and command lines with captures bound to the enrolled one, is not affected.
findings.requiredChange:
Test the maintenance target the way systemd reads it: over every word of the command line, after unquoting, with the last systemd.unit= winning.
- Refuse an ENROLLED entry in which any systemd.unit= or rd.systemd.unit= names the maintenance target.
- Require the MAINTENANCE entry's effective (last) systemd.unit= to be that target.
- Keep lockdown=integrity as a test on kernel parameters only, before the first bare "--" as next_arg tokenises the line. The simplest way to make a space split equal next_arg is to refuse '"' in kernelCmdline through the schema pattern.
- Add vectors for W6-a, W6-b and W6-e, and restate the README K1 row.
- Optional: without Secure Boot, systemd v256 also reads systemd.unit= from the SystemdOptions EFI variable (src/basic/efivars.c). /proc/cmdline overrides it only if it names a unit itself. Either require the ENROLLED entry to name its own target, or list this among the K1 limits.

findings.location: vectors.json positive[0..3].record.bootEntries and the command-line values of V38, V42, V47-V49; README K1 row ('its options line plus the initrd= it adds')
findings.finding:
systemd-boot v256 does not produce the positives' command lines.
- initrd_prepare (src/boot/efi/boot.c) builds the load options as 'initrd=<path> [initrd=<path> ...] <entry options>', so initrd= comes first.
- image_start may also append the SMBIOS string io.systemd.boot.kernel-cmdline-extra on non-confidential VMs.
The positives put initrd= after the options ('... lockdown=integrity initrd=\planeon\initrd-6.12.img'). No rule depends on the order: probe W6-f, with initrd= first, is accepted. So this is fixture plausibility only. Round-1 W6's request to make the positives consistent with the named loader is met only in part: BOOT_IMAGE= is gone.
findings.requiredChange: Put initrd= first in the positives and the derived vectors. Mention in the K1 row that systemd-boot can append the SMBIOS kernel-cmdline-extra string, which then appears in /proc/cmdline.

findings.location: scripts/native_qualification_v3.py check_record native-only rule (lines 341-343); README 'P1: role closures' row and W4 disposition
findings.finding:
The two native-only rules are uneven. The enrolled interpreter executable is refused by path or by content. The interpreter's installation tree is refused only by path prefix.
Probe W4-a: SERVER lists /opt/planeon/python/3.12.14/lib/libpython3.12.so.1.0, which is allowed. EFFECT_GATE lists /opt/planeon/lib/libpython3.12.so.1.0, with the same sha256 and verity, at its own inode. check_qualification ACCEPTS this.
The README residual says 'a Python runtime installed elsewhere ... is not recognised by the data'. That does not fit this case, because the record itself carries this content under the tree path. Exploiting it still needs the gate's own enrolled binary to load the library, so the risk stays low.
findings.requiredChange: In native-only closures, also refuse any file whose sha256 or verity equals that of a record file under INTERPRETER_TREE, and add a vector. Otherwise, state in the README that the tree rule works by path only.

findings.location: vectors.json V41, L11, L12, L14, V43, V44; scripts/native_qualification_v3.py check_lifecycle_capture (lines 525, 531) and check_qualification inode rule (lines 603-611); README 'Files' ('each pinned to its exact refused rule')

Mutation replay shows that two rules are not pinned by any vector.
(a) Deleting the 'one path, one (device, inode)' half of the inode rule leaves the 4 positives and all 216 cases with their pinned results. The model does refuse python3.12 at (123, 2004) in SERVER and (123, 2005) in WORKER, but with the message 'one inode reported for two files'.
(b) Deleting the enrolled-cgroups-in-census rule also leaves every case passing. V41 removes the gate cgroup but keeps sliceDescendants at 7, so the new nr_descendants rule refuses it with the same message, 'planeon slice census incomplete'. With sliceDescendants 6, the model refuses V41 and the mutant accepts it.
(c) L11, L12 and L14 add census entries without raising sliceDescendants, so each of them carries two defects.
The 'exact refused rule' claim is therefore weaker than stated.

findings.location: README caller obligation 3; scripts/native_qualification_v3.py module docstring (inspector obligation)
findings.finding:
Obligation 3 has the inspector read a role cgroup while it is frozen. For the probe-worker leaf, W01 §5.4 W1-W6 makes cgroup.freeze part of the broker's own lifecycle: freeze before clone3, thaw at W4, freeze before the kill at W6. An inspector that writes the leaf's cgroup.freeze could thaw a leaf the broker froze, or freeze the child during its pre-exec steps.
cgroup v2 freezes a cgroup when that cgroup or any ancestor is frozen (Documentation/admin-guide/cgroup-v2.rst, cgroup.freeze). So an inspector can freeze an ancestor without touching the leaf's own setting.
findings.requiredChange: State that the inspector freezes through an ancestor it controls, or reads while the broker holds the leaf frozen, and never writes the broker-owned leaf's cgroup.freeze. Carry this to the W02e/W03 inspector policy.

questionAnswers.Q3:
All four facts hold in Linux v6.12, and the four README digests match the files at tag v6.12.
- Attach types: the 22 census types plus the 7 hooks are disjoint, and their union equals to_cgroup_bpf_attach_type's 28 types plus BPF_LSM_CGROUP. That set is exactly the uapi enum's 29 cgroup types.
- Effective query: __cgroup_bpf_query with BPF_F_QUERY_EFFECTIVE reads cgrp->bpf.effective. compute_effective_progs includes an ancestor's programs when the ancestor has BPF_F_ALLOW_MULTI, or when no nearer program exists. For BPF_LSM_CGROUP the query spans CGROUP_LSM_START..END, which is 10 slots with CONFIG_BPF_LSM and none without it. BPF_PROG_QUERY is command 16.
- pids.current: it is charged in pids_can_fork for every copy_process and uncharged in pids_release, which release_task reaches through cgroup_release. So it counts tasks. The cgroup-v2 documentation also notes that migration can push pids.current above pids.max; refusing that is appropriate.
- /proc/<pid>/exe: exec_binprm swaps bprm->file for bprm->interpreter, begin_new_exec calls set_mm_exe_file, and proc_exe_link reads the exe file, so the link names the interpreter.
New facts used in round 2 also hold:
- cgroup.stat nr_descendants counts live descendants at every depth (cgroup_create increments every ancestor; cgroup_destroy_locked moves the count to nr_dying_descendants).
- /proc/cmdline is saved_command_line, with bootconfig kernel keys prepended and init.* keys after ' -- '.
- parse_args stops at a bare "--".
- next_arg honours double quotes.
- The socket-attached runners select the socket's cgroup; device, sysctl and LSM current select current's.

This is a source-level, DATA_CHECK_ONLY review of the five subject files at commit 761c9b8 (tree e9487d40). The files were hash-verified at the start and end of the review.
It establishes no native qualification and no kernel, SELinux, cgroup, BPF, boot-loader, systemd or TPM behaviour. It establishes no installed profile, selected distribution, seccomp filter or E01-E12 obligation, and it authorizes nothing.
The kernel and systemd facts come from reading the v6.12 and systemd v256 sources, not from running them.

The out-of-subject working-tree edits were not reviewed. Only the repository, my scratch directory and public source URLs were accessed. No GitHub, runner, sudo, cloud, native or warm-source action was taken.
